findings.scenario: Owner picks DP03 option C and follows the S17 prep card literally: talks to Arrg at 48/48 HP with Protect from Missiles on and runs from the arena centre to the safespot. Arrg 'primarily uses' his 38 melee (F-3089 quote) and that attack is NOT blocked by Protect from Missiles, so the prayer the card mandates protects against the less likely attack during the only phase where melee can reach. At Defence 1 a 38 lands from full HP: 48 -> 10. The card's rule is 'eat whenever HP is 30 or lower' and 'if a hit of 30+ lands before you reach the safespot, eat at once, then keep moving', with food described only as 'best healing food you have (16+)'. One ordinary food (owner Cooking 23) takes 10 HP to roughly 20-30, and the next attack 4 ticks later (attack speed 4, F-5021) is either another 38 melee (kills) or a 30 ranged that can occasionally pass prayer (kills at 30 or less). The card also sets the eat threshold at 30, which is wrong while melee can still reach: at 31-38 HP a single 38 kills. The risk officer's own verdict concedes 'no verified mitigation closes' the window, yet the step is approved and offered as option C with a card that implies it is survivable. The run's length and whether a teleport works in the arena are both undocumented (F-2036 caveat, bailout text), so the number of attacks taken during the run is unbounded by any fact.

findings.recommendation: Risk Officer: rewrite the S17 run phase. (1) While Arrg can still reach in melee, the eat threshold must be 38, not 30, and a single eat must be able to lift HP from 10 to 39+: require a combo-eat capable of 29+ healing in one tick-window (e.g. a hard food plus a cooked karambwan, buyable on the HW GE) and state the minimum heal per food, or state honestly that the card cannot survive two max hits and that option C relies on hit RNG during the run. (2) Decide which prayer to hold during the run from evidence (melee primary but inaccurate vs ranged accurate) and say why; switching to Protect from Missiles only once at the melee safespot is the documented logic. (3) Raise an RFI for the run length in ticks and arena teleport behaviour, and for whether an escape crystal configured to the minimum inactivity timer fires in the arena (it does not fire while moving, so it does not cover the run itself). (4) Route Strategist: DP03 option C must quote the unclosed window in its cons, not only 'most dangerous required fight'.

findings.scenario: On the default (balanced) route the owner obeys the S12 prep card, which lists a ring of life as a required item and mitigation S12-M1 'Wear a ring of life in the Koschei fight'. The wiki the card itself cites says the opposite: 'Do not wear a ring of life as you will be teleported back to your spawn point. You will need to fight him again at his first phase.' Form 4 hits 1 HP every tick and ends the fight only at 1 HP (F-5002, F-5009); a ring of life worn into form 4 fires as soon as HP falls below 10% (about 4 HP at 48 max), so the owner is teleported out and Koschei resets to form 1 every time. A literal follower cannot finish the quest while obeying the card, and every retry re-exposes him to forms 1-3, the only run-ending phases (F-5001), with no armour. The mitigation is also credited with escape -2, which drops the step's residual; that credit is invalid for form 4 and overstated for forms 1-3 (the ring cannot save from a hit that kills outright).

findings.scenario: LADDER: the isotonic fit collapses most of the mid-ladder. Ladder points include (66, 54.8) and (82, 54.8): every model score from 66 to 82 publishes as ~55, so Zulrah learner (pos 66), ToA entry/normal (70), Barrows (50), Werewolf (49), Elvarg (48) and the Wilderness Agility Course (46) become indistinguishable, and the fit has cliffs of +17 published points for model 63->66 and +18 for 82->84. Cause: model saturation (T5 with any C factor of 5, typically disconnect 5) puts Jad, the Inferno, the Colosseum, ToB HM and the Revenant Caves all at raw 94, and the ladder was approved with five unresolved ordering conflicts that validate.py itself warns about. In the guide, S16 Troll Stronghold inherent publishes 94 'Extreme' and S24 94, above Phosani's Nightmare (87) and ToA expert (88): a quest scored like a top-end raid. A one-step change in any factor near these cliffs moves a published score by 0 or by ~17 points.

findings.scenario: LADDER: the Wilderness premium is added on top of board positions that already price in PvP, so it double-counts. revs-pvp was placed at 76 because it is 'a designed PK hotspot with teleblock'; +20 publishes it at 96, level with the Inferno and above ToB Hard Mode (92), ToA expert (88) and Phosani (87). The Wilderness Agility Course (46, 'deep-Wilderness PvP with no teleport') publishes 66, above Jad (62) and Zulrah learner (66 tie). Also: (a) the fallback treats a step flagged only WILDERNESS as level 1 (+5), the least conservative choice, so a step missing its wilderness_level and DEEP flag in level 50 gets +5 instead of +20; (b) the premium follows residual flags, so a mitigation that removes the WILDERNESS flag also removes the premium; (c) the policy's status line still says 'with wilderness premium +25' although the owner replaced it with tiers. No step in this guide enters the Wilderness, so nothing in the route is affected today.

findings.scenario: Underground Pass, Iban's temple: entering the temple triggers red spikes near the entrance that 'rapidly deal around 5 to 8 damage each and can't be blocked with prayers. They also stun you and teleport you back to the entrance, so make sure you run in with plenty of health.' The S05 prep card gates HP at 40+ only for bridge jumps, the rope swing and Kalrag; the only general stop condition is 'teleport out if HP < 25 and food is gone'. Spike damage is not reduced by Protect from Melee, the prayer the card relies on at that stage.

findings.scenario: Disconnect mitigation not used: every Hardcore Worlds character starts with an escape crystal (F-3016), and the current wiki says it can be configured to auto-teleport on taking damage after 2-300 s of inactivity. The plan lists the crystal in its checklist, but no DISCONNECT_FATAL step (S06 Tyras guard, S12 Koschei forms 2-3, S16 generals, S17 Arrg) credits or even mentions it, while those steps rate disconnect at 4-5 or remove the flag by prayer alone. findings.scenario: Random events: the plan's mitigation ('long rooftop sessions should be broken up and HP kept high') and the rooftop factor rationales ('random events' as unpredictability) aim at the wrong mechanism. The current wiki says random events can be dismissed or ignored and disappear after a minute; aggressive random events were removed in 2014 'without a risk of dying'. The realistic Hardcore Worlds trap is different: accepting a teleporting event while in a dangerous place (Underground Pass, Trollheim, Isafdar, Darkmeyer) returns the player to the same tile among the same aggressive monsters, or to Lumbridge if the tile became blocked; and an event interface opened mid-fight costs attention. HP level does not mitigate either.

findings.scenario: New with the RT-11 fix (S12-M6). A literal follower who carries the escape crystal in the inventory, set to a short inactivity timer as M6 suggests, reaches Koschei's form 4 and obeys the bailout text 'Form 4: do not resist; let him take you to 1 HP'. Form 4 hits 1 every tick (F-5009), so a player who stands still takes damage after the inactivity time and the crystal fires (F-3017): he is teleported out and the fight restarts at form 1 (F-5011, F-0015), which re-exposes him to the run-ending forms 1-3. M6 itself says 'keep walking' in form 4 so it cannot fire, but the bailout and stop conditions do not, and the crystal earns no credit anywhere in the duel, so carrying it adds a reset loop and no counted protection.
